title: combine f' and f'' for graph features
stem: A function f has f'(x)=1(x−(-3))(x−(1)) for all real x, with -3<1. Which set of features belongs in an accurate sketch of f?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A local minimum at x=-3, a local maximum at x=1, and an inflection at x=-1.
choices.rationale: The first derivative sign changes at both zeros are reversed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A local maximum at x=-3, a local minimum at x=1, and an inflection at x=-1 where f is decreasing.
choices.rationale: Correct: f' has signs positive, negative, positive across -3,1. Also f''=1(2x−(-3)−(1)) changes sign at -1; f'(-1) has sign negative.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inflection points at both x=-3 and x=1 because f' is zero there, with no local extrema.
choices.rationale: Zeros of f' classify extrema of f; f'' changes sign at the midpoint, not at both derivative zeros.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No inflection point, because the given first derivative is a quadratic polynomial.
choices.rationale: The derivative of the quadratic f' is linear and changes sign at its zero, producing an inflection of f.

title: translate derivative table into local sketch
stem: A table from a twice-differentiable function records f'(-3)=5, f''(-3)=-6, f'(1)=-3, and f''(1)=2. A student is drawing local pieces of the graph near x=-3 and x=1. Which annotations match the table?

choices.label: A
choices.text: f is rising at both points because f'' is nonzero at both.
choices.rationale: A nonzero second derivative controls concavity, not whether f is rising; one listed f' is negative.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Near x=-3, f is rising and concave down; near x=1, f is falling and concave up.
choices.rationale: Correct: f' signs at -3,1 are 5,-3, setting rise/fall; f'' signs are -6,2, setting concavity. Neither f' value is zero.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Near x=-3, f is falling, and near x=1, f is rising; the f' values give the opposite slope signs.
choices.rationale: This reverses the sign interpretation of f' at both sampled points.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both sampled points must be local extrema of f because f'' is nonzero at each.
choices.rationale: A nonzero f' rules out a differentiable local extremum at these sampled points.

title: translate derivative table into local sketch (variant 1)
stem: A twice-differentiable function has f'(-1)=-3, f''(-1)=-2, f'(3)=5, and f''(3)=6. For a sufficiently small neighborhood of each point, compare the graph with its tangent line there. Which pair of sketch notes is justified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At x=-1, the tangent slopes down and lies locally above the graph; at x=3, it slopes up and lies locally below the graph.
choices.rationale: Correct: f' gives tangent slopes -3,5. Negative f'' puts a graph below its tangent locally; positive f'' puts a graph above it. The tangent sides are above,below.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The tangent slopes have the same signs as stated, but lie below the graph near x=-1 and above the graph near x=3.
choices.rationale: This reverses the local tangent-versus-graph relation implied by each nonzero second derivative.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tangent lies on the stated side of the graph at each point, but its slope signs are the reverse of the listed f' values.
choices.rationale: The sign of f' directly gives each tangent slope; these slope directions are reversed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tangent must cross the graph at both points because both second derivatives are nonzero.
choices.rationale: Nonzero second derivative makes the tangent stay on one local side of the graph rather than cross it immediately.

title: classify stationary inflection and local extremum
stem: A differentiable function g has g'(x)=1(x−(-2))²(x−(4)) for all real x. A proposed sketch marks x=-2 as a horizontal tangent and x=4 as another horizontal tangent. Which additional classification is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: x=-2 and x=4 are both local minimum points because g' vanishes at both.
choices.rationale: A repeated derivative zero does not change g' sign, while the simple zero does.

choices.label: B
choices.text: x=-2 is a stationary inflection, but x=4 is also an inflection because g' vanishes there.
choices.rationale: The simple zero of g' is an extremum of g, not an inflection; g'' does not vanish there.

choices.label: C
choices.text: x=-2 is a stationary inflection, x=2 is another inflection, and x=4 is a local minimum.
choices.rationale: Correct: The squared factor makes g' keep its sign at -2; the simple factor changes sign at 4, giving a local minimum. Differentiation gives g''=1(x−(-2))(3x−(6)), whose signs change at -2 and 2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: x=2 is a local minimum of g because it is a zero of g''.
choices.rationale: A zero of g'' can signal an inflection of g, not a local extremum unless g' also changes sign.
